title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 40 (Securities to be dealt with in stock exchanges)

content.overview: Section 40 requires every company making a public offer, before making such offer, to apply to one or more recognised stock exchanges and obtain permission for the securities to be dealt with there. Where the prospectus states that such an application has been made, it must name the stock exchange(s). All public application monies must be kept in a separate bank account in a scheduled bank and may be used only for adjustment against allotment where permission has been obtained, or for repayment within the time specified by SEBI where the company is unable to allot. Any waiver of compliance is void. Default attracts fine on the company (₹5 lakh to ₹50 lakh) and on every officer in default (₹50,000 to ₹3 lakh); the imprisonment limb for officers was omitted by the 2020 Amendment. Commission in connection with subscription may be paid subject to prescribed conditions.
content.glance: Pre-offer stock-exchange application and permission; prospectus naming of exchange(s); segregated public application money; waiver void; fine-based default (no officer imprisonment after 2020 Amendment).
content.study: Before a public offer the company must apply to one or more recognised stock exchanges and obtain permission for the securities to be dealt with there. If the prospectus states that the application has been made, it must state the name(s) of the stock exchange(s). Public application monies must be kept in a separate scheduled-bank account and may be used only (a) for adjustment against allotment where the securities have been permitted to be dealt with on the named exchange(s), or (b) for repayment within the SEBI-specified time where the company is unable to allot. Any condition requiring an applicant to waive compliance is void. Contravention attracts the statutory fines (company ₹5 lakh–₹50 lakh; officer ₹50,000–₹3 lakh); imprisonment of officers was removed by Act 29 of 2020. Commission may be paid subject to prescribed conditions. Current-law framing: identify public offer; test pre-offer permission; check prospectus disclosure and money segregation/use; apply current penalty text.

sections.heading: Pre-offer exchange application and permission
sections.body: Every company making a public offer shall, before making such offer, apply to one or more recognised stock exchanges and obtain permission for the securities to be dealt with there.

sections.heading: Prospectus disclosure
sections.body: Where the prospectus states that an application under sub-section (1) has been made, it shall also state the name or names of the stock exchange(s) in which the securities shall be dealt with.

sections.heading: Separate bank account and restricted use
sections.body: All monies received on application from the public shall be kept in a separate bank account in a scheduled bank and shall not be utilised for any purpose other than (a) adjustment against allotment where permission has been obtained for the named exchange(s), or (b) repayment within the time specified by SEBI where the company is unable to allot.

sections.heading: Waiver void
sections.body: Any condition purporting to require or bind any applicant to waive compliance with any requirement of this section shall be void.

sections.heading: Penalty and commission
sections.body: Default: company fine ₹5 lakh to ₹50 lakh; every officer in default fine ₹50,000 to ₹3 lakh (imprisonment limb omitted by 2020 Amendment). Commission may be paid subject to prescribed conditions.

provisions.title: Securities to be dealt with in stock exchanges

examples.title: Pre-offer permission required
examples.body: A company proposes a public offer but has not obtained recognised-stock-exchange permission. The public offer cannot proceed on the theory that permission can be obtained later.

examples.title: Segregated application money
examples.body: Application money collected into a general operating account and spent on unrelated expenses conflicts with the statutory segregation and use restriction.

examples.title: Waiver condition void
examples.body: An application form that requires the subscriber to waive section 40 compliance is void to that extent.

misconceptions.trap: Later exchange permission cures a pre-offer failure to apply.
misconceptions.correction: Section 40(1) requires application and permission before the public offer.

misconceptions.trap: Public application money may be used for general expenses.
misconceptions.correction: Money must stay in a separate scheduled-bank account and may be used only as section 40(3) allows.

misconceptions.trap: Officers still face imprisonment under section 40(5).
misconceptions.correction: The imprisonment limb was omitted by Act 29 of 2020; only fine remains for officers.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should section 40 be analysed on public-offer facts?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify whether a public offer is being made. II. Test pre-offer application and permission, prospectus naming of exchange(s), and money segregation/use. III. Note void-waiver rule and current fine-only officer penalty. IV. Conclude.
